OpenCV.Features.Correspondences.name: Point_Correspondence
Point_Correspondence_Array
OpenCV.Features.Correspondences.signature:
--  Ordinary Ada array of candidate correspondences. From_Matches returns
   --  bounds 1 .. Matches'Length, in input order.
   type Point_Correspondence_Array is
     array (Positive range <>) of Point_Correspondence;

OpenCV.Features.Correspondences.name: From_Matches
OpenCV.Features.Correspondences.signature:
--  Pure Ada value copy using only public Count/Point accessors. Validate
   --  every one-based query/train index before constructing the result;
   --  an index beyond its feature count raises OpenCV_Error.
   --  Return bounds are 1 .. Matches'Length, including 1 .. 0 for any empty
   --  Matches (even with empty feature sets or different descriptor norms).
   --  Preserve input order and all duplicates, indices and descriptor distances
   --  exactly. Norm compatibility and norm-specific distance validation are
   --  deliberately not required for manually supplied matches.
   --  Copy stored Float32 positions without arithmetic, rounding, normalization,
   --  offsets or coordinate-frame/Region reinterpretation. Distance is metadata,
   --  not confidence, probability, geometric residual or reprojection error.
   --  Inputs are unchanged; returned ordinary Ada values retain no references
   --  to features, detectors, Mats or native storage. No matching/filtering or
   --  geometric verification occurs: these are candidates, not geometric inliers.
   --  Normal Ada allocation exceptions remain possible for array results.
   --  Matches can come from Nearest, Mutual_Nearest, ratio-filtered KNN2 or
   --  radius matching, or be supplied manually, provided they refer to these
   --  same Query and Train sets. Raw two-nearest candidates are not accepted;
   --  select matches first, for example with Filter_By_Ratio.
   --  @param Query Feature set that the matches' Query_Index values refer to.
   --  @param Train Feature set that the matches' Train_Index values refer to.
   --  @param Matches Accepted matches, with any index bounds; each
   --  Query_Index must be at most Count (Query) and each Train_Index at most
   --  Count (Train).
   --  @return One correspondence per match, in the same order, with bounds
   --  1 .. Matches'Length.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error A Query_Index exceeds Count (Query) or a
   --  Train_Index exceeds Count (Train); nothing is returned in that case.
   function From_Matches
     (Query   : Feature_Set;
      Train   : Feature_Set;
      Matches : Matching.Descriptor_Match_Array)
      return Point_Correspondence_Array;

OpenCV.Features.Matching.name: Matching_Mode
OpenCV.Features.Matching.signature:
--  Selection rule for one-best matching (Brute_Force_Match).
   --  @enum Nearest For every query descriptor, the train descriptor at
   --  minimum distance (OpenCV BFMatcher without cross-check). Every query
   --  gets one match when both sets are nonempty; train indices may repeat.
   --  @enum Mutual_Nearest OpenCV BFMatcher cross-check: a query's nearest
   --  train descriptor is kept only when that query is also the train
   --  descriptor's nearest query. Queries without a mutual partner are
   --  omitted; query and train indices are each unique. This symmetric
   --  consistency check is not a ratio test.
   type Matching_Mode is (Nearest, Mutual_Nearest);

OpenCV.Features.Matching.name: Binary_Descriptor_Distance
Descriptor_Match
Descriptor_Match_Array
OpenCV.Features.Matching.signature:
--  Ordinary Ada array of matches. Matching operations return bounds
   --  1 .. N, including 1 .. 0 for an empty result.
   type Descriptor_Match_Array is
     array (Positive range <>) of Descriptor_Match;

OpenCV.Features.Matching.name: Brute_Force_Match
OpenCV.Features.Matching.signature:
--  One-based indices map to descriptor rows/keypoints (1 -> native row 0).
   --  Results are ordinary owned Ada values, in ascending Query_Index order.
   --  Norms must agree, even for empty sets: WTA2 uses Hamming (0..256),
   --  WTA3/4 uses Hamming2 (0..128), with exact integer distances.
   --  Nearest returns Count(Query) entries if both sets are nonempty; ties
   --  do not promise a particular Train_Index. Mutual_Nearest uses native
   --  cross-check, with unique query/train indices; it is NOT a ratio test.
   --  Compatible empty inputs return (1 .. 0). Train.Count > 262143 raises
   --  OpenCV_Error (native BFMatcher packs train indices into 18 bits).
   --  No masks, confidence score or geometric verification.
   --  Inputs are borrowed, not copied or modified. Concurrent mutation through
   --  implementation interfaces is not supported. Large results allocate an
   --  array function result; normal Ada allocation exceptions remain possible.
   --  @param Query Feature set whose descriptors are matched; in Nearest
   --  mode every query keypoint receives exactly one match.
   --  @param Train Feature set searched for the nearest descriptors; at most
   --  262143 keypoints. There is no corresponding 18-bit limit on Query.
   --  @param Mode Nearest (the default) or Mutual_Nearest.
   --  @return Matches with strictly ascending Query_Index and bounds 1 .. N:
   --  N = Count (Query) for Nearest with two nonempty sets, N <=
   --  Count (Query) for Mutual_Nearest, and N = 0 when either set is empty.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error The two norms differ (also for empty sets),
   --  Train has more than 262143 keypoints, or native matching fails.
   function Brute_Force_Match
     (Query : Feature_Set; Train : Feature_Set;
      Mode : Matching_Mode := Nearest) return Descriptor_Match_Array;

OpenCV.Features.Matching.name: Binary_Neighbor
Brute_Force_Radius_Match
OpenCV.Features.Matching.signature:
--  Absolute inclusive radius, not KNN/ratio filtering or cross-check.
   --  Norms must agree, even for empty inputs; automatic Hamming for WTA2,
   --  Hamming2 for WTA3/4. OpenCV_Error unless Maximum_Distance is 1..256
   --  (Hamming) or 1..128 (Hamming2), including empty inputs. Zero is rejected;
   --  exact-zero radius matching is deferred, not mapped to another radius.
   --  Compatible empties return (1 .. 0); one-row Train is valid.
   --  All qualifying matches, flat and Ada-owned: ascending Query_Index,
   --  nondecreasing Distance within each query, unspecified tied train order.
   --  Query/train indices are one-based and bounded by the input counts;
   --  each train row occurs at most once per query, not once globally.
   --  Queries can contribute zero, one, or many matches; length need not equal
   --  Query.Count. Distances are exact integers, <= Maximum_Distance.
   --  No KNN 18-bit train bound: native rows/indices are signed 32-bit; flat
   --  count must fit signed 32-bit and Ada Natural/allocation representation.
   --  Inputs unchanged; owned values survive inputs, detector and native staging.
   --  CPU Mats only; no masks, persistent matcher or geometric policy. Native
   --  full distance matrices/results may be large; allocation can fail.
   --  OpenCV itself rejects radii that are not above floating-point epsilon
   --  for nonempty inputs, so the binding rejects zero for every input
   --  instead of silently substituting a different radius.
   --  @param Query Feature set whose descriptors are matched.
   --  @param Train Feature set searched within the radius; no 18-bit row
   --  limit applies.
   --  @param Maximum_Distance Inclusive absolute distance limit chosen by
   --  the caller: 1 .. 256 for Hamming sets, 1 .. 128 for Hamming_2 sets.
   --  There is no default.
   --  @return Every pair with distance <= Maximum_Distance, grouped by
   --  ascending Query_Index, with bounds 1 .. N; 1 .. 0 when nothing
   --  qualifies or either set is empty.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error The norms differ, Maximum_Distance is zero or
   --  above the norm's maximum (checked also for empty inputs), or native
   --  matching or allocation fails.
   function Brute_Force_Radius_Match
     (Query : Feature_Set; Train : Feature_Set;
      Maximum_Distance : Binary_Descriptor_Distance)
      return Descriptor_Match_Array;

OpenCV.Features.Matching.name: Two_Nearest_Match
Two_Nearest_Match_Array
OpenCV.Features.Matching.signature:
--  Ordinary Ada array of two-nearest candidates. Brute_Force_KNN_2
   --  returns one per query keypoint, with bounds 1 .. N.
   type Two_Nearest_Match_Array is
     array (Positive range <>) of Two_Nearest_Match;

OpenCV.Features.Matching.name: Brute_Force_KNN_2
OpenCV.Features.Matching.signature:
--  Exactly K=2, without cross-check. Norm compatibility is checked before
   --  empties. Compatible empties return (1 .. 0); a nonempty query with one
   --  train row raises OpenCV_Error. Train.Count <= 262143; no corresponding
   --  18-bit Query limit. Otherwise Length = Query.Count, in ascending query
   --  order. One-based train indices are distinct, nearest distance <= second,
   --  exact Hamming 0..256 / Hamming2 0..128. Ties have no fixed train ordering.
   --  Owned Ada values survive all inputs and native staging. Inputs unchanged.
   --  The result carries candidates only; apply an explicit caller policy,
   --  such as Filter_By_Ratio, before using pairs as matches.
   --  @param Query Feature set whose descriptors are matched.
   --  @param Train Feature set searched for two neighbors; it needs at least
   --  two keypoints when Query is nonempty, and at most 262143.
   --  @return One candidate per query keypoint, with Query_Index I at
   --  position I and bounds 1 .. Count (Query); 1 .. 0 when either set is
   --  empty.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error The norms differ (also for empty sets), Train
   --  has more than 262143 keypoints, a nonempty Query meets a one-keypoint
   --  Train, or native matching fails.
   function Brute_Force_KNN_2
     (Query : Feature_Set; Train : Feature_Set)
      return Two_Nearest_Match_Array;

OpenCV.Features.Matching.name: Passes_Ratio_Test
OpenCV.Features.Matching.signature:
--  Pure Ada mechanics, no default application policy. OpenCV_Error unless
   --  0 < Maximum_Ratio < 1 (also rejects NaN/nonfinite). Strict acceptance:
   --  nearest < Maximum_Ratio * second, using floating integer conversion.
   --  Thus 0/0 duplicate descriptors reject. Ratio is not confidence/probability.
   --  The test only compares the two distances of one query as a
   --  distinctiveness heuristic; its outcome depends on the caller's
   --  threshold and is not a calibrated likelihood. A zero nearest distance
   --  passes whenever the second distance is nonzero.
   --  @param Candidate Two-nearest candidate to test.
   --  @param Maximum_Ratio Caller-chosen threshold, strictly between 0 and 1.
   --  @return True when Nearest.Distance < Maximum_Ratio *
   --  Second_Nearest.Distance.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error Maximum_Ratio is not in the open interval
   --  0 .. 1, including NaN and infinities.
   function Passes_Ratio_Test
     (Candidate : Two_Nearest_Match; Maximum_Ratio : OpenCV.Float64_Value)
      return Boolean;

OpenCV.Features.Matching.name: Filter_By_Ratio
OpenCV.Features.Matching.signature:
--  Returns nearest matches only, preserving candidate order. Validates the
   --  threshold even for empty input; empty/all-rejected returns (1 .. 0).
   --  No native calls or geometric verification. Normal Ada allocation errors
   --  remain possible for array results, as for Brute_Force_Match.
   --  @param Candidates Two-nearest candidates, normally from
   --  Brute_Force_KNN_2.
   --  @param Maximum_Ratio Caller-chosen threshold, strictly between 0 and 1;
   --  applied to every candidate exactly as Passes_Ratio_Test.
   --  @return The Query_Index, Nearest.Train_Index and Nearest.Distance of
   --  each accepted candidate, in candidate order, with bounds 1 .. N.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error Maximum_Ratio is not in the open interval
   --  0 .. 1, including NaN and infinities, even for empty Candidates.
   function Filter_By_Ratio
     (Candidates : Two_Nearest_Match_Array;
      Maximum_Ratio : OpenCV.Float64_Value) return Descriptor_Match_Array;

OpenCV.Features.ORB.name: Tuple_Size
OpenCV.Features.ORB.signature:
--  Number of points compared to build each descriptor element (OpenCV
   --  WTA_K). It also selects the norm recorded in the result.
   --  @enum Two_Samples WTA_K = 2, the default; descriptors use Hamming.
   --  @enum Three_Samples WTA_K = 3; descriptors use Hamming_2.
   --  @enum Four_Samples WTA_K = 4; descriptors use Hamming_2.
   type Tuple_Size is (Two_Samples, Three_Samples, Four_Samples);

OpenCV.Features.ORB.name: Score_Kind
OpenCV.Features.ORB.signature:
--  Measure used to rank FAST keypoint candidates before the strongest
   --  are retained. It also determines the meaning of Keypoint.Response.
   --  @enum Harris_Score Rank by the Harris corner response (OpenCV
   --  HARRIS_SCORE); the default.
   --  @enum FAST_Score Rank by the FAST score (OpenCV FAST_SCORE).
   type Score_Kind is (Harris_Score, FAST_Score);

OpenCV.Features.ORB.name: Configuration
OpenCV.Features.ORB.signature:
--  Public ORB parameters. Create validates the ranges that the Ada
   --  subtypes do not express and rejects others with OpenCV_Error.
   --  @field Maximum_Features Requested feature target (OpenCV nfeatures),
   --  1 .. 1_073_741_823 (2_147_483_647 / 2), default 500. It is a target
   --  distributed over the pyramid levels, not a strict cap: a result can
   --  hold fewer keypoints, or more when native responses tie.
   --  @field Tuple WTA_K selection, default Two_Samples.
   --  @field Score Candidate ranking measure, default Harris_Score.
   --  @field FAST_Threshold FAST intensity-difference threshold (OpenCV
   --  fastThreshold), 0 .. 255, default 20; larger values make corner
   --  detection stricter.
   type Configuration is record
      Maximum_Features : Positive := 500;
      Tuple            : Tuple_Size := Two_Samples;
      Score            : Score_Kind := Harris_Score;
      FAST_Threshold   : Natural := 20;
   end record;

OpenCV.Features.ORB.name: Detector
OpenCV.Features.ORB.signature:
--  Owner of one native ORB detector, configured with a Configuration and
   --  a deliberately small initial profile. Native structural parameters are
   --  fixed at scaleFactor=1.2f, nlevels=8, edgeThreshold=31, firstLevel=0,
   --  patchSize=31. Expanding that surface is a later reviewed slice.
   --  A default-declared Detector is not ready; Create returns a ready one.
   --  Close and finalization release the native detector; both are
   --  idempotent and never raise. Detectors are limited and cannot be
   --  copied. Feature sets produced by a detector remain valid after it is
   --  closed or finalized.
   type Detector is tagged limited private;

OpenCV.Features.ORB.name: Create
OpenCV.Features.ORB.signature:
--  Create a ready detector with the given parameters and the fixed
   --  structural profile.
   --  @param Parameters Requested configuration; all defaults when omitted.
   --  @return A ready detector owning its native ORB instance.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error Maximum_Features exceeds 1_073_741_823,
   --  FAST_Threshold exceeds 255, or the native detector cannot be created.
   function Create (Parameters : Configuration := (others => <>))
      return Detector;

OpenCV.Features.ORB.name: Close
OpenCV.Features.ORB.signature:
--  Release the native detector early. Closing a default-declared or
   --  already closed detector has no effect. Afterwards Is_Ready is False,
   --  and Parameters and Detect_And_Compute raise OpenCV_Error. Existing
   --  feature sets are unaffected. Do not close a detector while another
   --  task is extracting with it.
   --  @param Self Detector to close.
   procedure Close (Self : in out Detector);

OpenCV.Features.ORB.name: Is_Ready
OpenCV.Features.ORB.signature:
--  Whether the detector owns a native ORB instance, that is, it was
   --  returned by Create and has not been closed or finalized.
   --  @param Self Detector to inspect.
   --  @return True when extraction can be attempted.
   function Is_Ready (Self : Detector) return Boolean;

OpenCV.Features.ORB.name: Parameters
OpenCV.Features.ORB.signature:
--  Configuration that was supplied to Create, unchanged.
   --  @param Self A ready detector.
   --  @return The detector's public parameters.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error The detector is not ready.
   function Parameters (Self : Detector) return Configuration;

OpenCV.Features.ORB.name: Detect_And_Compute
OpenCV.Features.ORB.signature:
--  Detect ORB keypoints anywhere in the image and compute their binary
   --  descriptors. Image: nonempty UInt8 C1, two dimensions, at least 2x2.
   --  The fixed-profile native arithmetic envelope is checked in the shim;
   --  see docs/orb-contract.md. The image is snapshotted before native
   --  detection: a Region is an isolated logical image, returned coordinates
   --  are local to it, and a noncontiguous Region gives the same result as
   --  its packed clone. Inputs are unchanged on success and failure. A valid
   --  image without detectable features returns an empty set, not an error.
   --  Count of the result is the actual number produced, which can differ
   --  from Maximum_Features. Use distinct detectors for concurrent calls.
   --  Concurrent mutation of source storage, or Close during extraction, is
   --  not supported.
   --  @param Self A ready detector.
   --  @param Image Two-dimensional UInt8 single-channel image, at least 2x2
   --  and within the conservative native size envelope.
   --  @return A new feature set that owns its keypoints and descriptors and
   --  records the norm implied by the detector's Tuple.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error The detector is not ready, the image is
   --  empty, has the wrong type, rank or size, exceeds the native envelope,
   --  or the native extraction fails.
   function Detect_And_Compute
     (Self : Detector; Image : OpenCV.Core.Mat) return Feature_Set;

OpenCV.Features.ORB.name: Detect_And_Compute
OpenCV.Features.ORB.signature:
--  Detect only where Mask is nonzero, then describe the detected
   --  keypoints. The mask controls where keypoints may be detected; it does
   --  not restrict which pixels a descriptor patch samples. Mask must match
   --  the image geometry and type: a two-dimensional UInt8 single-channel
   --  Mat with the image's rows and columns. Image and mask are
   --  independently snapshotted; neither is modified.
   --  An all-zero mask yields an empty set. For portable results use only
   --  0 and 255. Other nonzero values are passed through unchanged. In the
   --  reviewed OpenCV 4.1.0 and 4.10.0 sources they count at pyramid level 0,
   --  but only 255 survives into later levels; OpenCV 5.0.0 first maps every
   --  nonzero value to 255. Thus an all-1 mask allows only octave-0 keypoints
   --  on those 4.x releases but behaves like an all-255 mask on 5.0. All
   --  other rules match the unmasked overload.
   --  @param Self A ready detector.
   --  @param Image Two-dimensional UInt8 single-channel image, at least 2x2
   --  and within the conservative native size envelope.
   --  @param Mask Detection mask with the same rows, columns and type as
   --  Image.
   --  @return A new feature set restricted to keypoints detected inside the
   --  mask.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error The detector is not ready, the image or
   --  mask is invalid, their geometries differ, the native envelope is
   --  exceeded, or the native extraction fails.
   function Detect_And_Compute
     (Self : Detector; Image, Mask : OpenCV.Core.Mat) return Feature_Set;

OpenCV.Features.name: Keypoint
OpenCV.Features.signature:
--  One detected keypoint, copied from the native result without
   --  normalization. Coordinates are local to the image or Region passed to
   --  the detector: X is the column and Y the row, in pixels from its first
   --  element. Before publication the native layer requires finite values,
   --  0 <= X < columns, 0 <= Y < rows, Size > 0 and a valid pyramid octave.
   --  Keypoints from a higher octave are rescaled to input pixels and need
   --  not have integral coordinates.
   --  @field Position Keypoint location (X column, Y row) in input pixels.
   --  @field Size Diameter of the keypoint neighborhood in input pixels, as
   --  reported by OpenCV; always finite and positive.
   --  @field Angle_Degrees Keypoint orientation in degrees, as computed by
   --  the native detector; finite, with no range normalization by Ada.
   --  @field Response Native detector response used to rank keypoints (the
   --  configured Harris or FAST score). It is preserved unchanged and is not
   --  a probability or match confidence.
   --  @field Octave Zero-based pyramid level that produced the keypoint; for
   --  the fixed ORB profile it is in 0 .. 7.
   --  @field Class_Id Native class identifier, preserved unchanged. The
   --  Features operations neither assign nor interpret it.
   type Keypoint is record
      Position      : OpenCV.Float32_Point;
      Size          : OpenCV.Float32_Value;
      Angle_Degrees : OpenCV.Float32_Value;
      Response      : OpenCV.Float32_Value;
      Octave        : OpenCV.Int32_Value;
      Class_Id      : OpenCV.Int32_Value;
   end record;

OpenCV.Features.name: Keypoint_Array
Binary_Descriptor_Norm
OpenCV.Features.signature:
--  Distance norm required to compare a set's binary descriptors. ORB
   --  WTA_K = 2 (Two_Samples) produces Hamming descriptors; WTA_K = 3 or 4
   --  produces Hamming_2 descriptors. Matching requires both sets to carry
   --  the same norm.
   --  @enum Hamming Number of differing bits across the 32-byte descriptor,
   --  0 .. 256 (OpenCV NORM_HAMMING).
   --  @enum Hamming_2 Number of differing 2-bit cells across the descriptor,
   --  0 .. 128 (OpenCV NORM_HAMMING2).
   type Binary_Descriptor_Norm is (Hamming, Hamming_2);

OpenCV.Features.name: Feature_Set
OpenCV.Features.signature:
--  An immutable, paired collection. Construction is through a detector.
   --  A default-declared set is empty. Results own their keypoint values and
   --  Core-owned descriptor storage, independently of the source/detector.
   --  Limited ownership avoids accidental copying of large feature sets.
   --  Keypoints are stored as Ada values in native detector order; keypoint
   --  I is paired with descriptor row I - 1. A set stays valid after its
   --  detector is closed or finalized and after the source image or mask is
   --  modified. No public operation changes a set after construction. A
   --  default-declared set reports the Hamming norm.
   type Feature_Set is limited private;

OpenCV.Features.name: Count
OpenCV.Features.signature:
--  Number of keypoints, equal to the number of descriptor rows. This is
   --  the actual produced count: it can be zero and is not bounded by a
   --  detector's requested feature target.
   --  @param Features Feature set to inspect.
   --  @return Number of stored keypoints.
   function Count (Features : Feature_Set) return Natural;

OpenCV.Features.name: Is_Empty
OpenCV.Features.signature:
--  True exactly when Count (Features) = 0, for example for a blank or
   --  fully masked image, or for a default-declared set.
   --  @param Features Feature set to inspect.
   --  @return Whether the set contains no keypoints.
   function Is_Empty (Features : Feature_Set) return Boolean;

OpenCV.Features.name: Point
OpenCV.Features.signature:
--  Copy of one stored keypoint, selected by its one-based index.
   --  @param Features Feature set to read.
   --  @param Index One-based keypoint index in 1 .. Count (Features).
   --  @return The keypoint value stored at Index.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error Index is greater than Count (Features).
   function Point (Features : Feature_Set; Index : Positive) return Keypoint;

OpenCV.Features.name: Keypoints
OpenCV.Features.signature:
--  Copy of every stored keypoint, in stored order.
   --  @param Features Feature set to read.
   --  @return An array with bounds 1 .. Count (Features); 1 .. 0 when empty.
   function Keypoints (Features : Feature_Set) return Keypoint_Array;

OpenCV.Features.name: Required_Norm
OpenCV.Features.signature:
--  Norm that must be used to compare these descriptors. It is recorded
   --  from the detector configuration, also for empty results.
   --  @param Features Feature set to inspect.
   --  @return Hamming for ORB Two_Samples results; Hamming_2 for
   --  Three_Samples and Four_Samples results.
   function Required_Norm
     (Features : Feature_Set) return Binary_Descriptor_Norm;

OpenCV.Features.name: Descriptor_Row
OpenCV.Features.signature:
--  Ada keypoint Index = 1 maps to OpenCV descriptor row 0. An invalid
   --  positive index raises OpenCV_Error (not a native unchecked access).
   --  @param Features Feature set whose pairing is queried.
   --  @param Index One-based keypoint index in 1 .. Count (Features).
   --  @return The zero-based descriptor row, Index - 1.
   --  @exception OpenCV_Error Index is greater than Count (Features).
   function Descriptor_Row
     (Features : Feature_Set; Index : Positive) return Natural;

OpenCV.Features.name: Descriptor_Copy
OpenCV.Features.signature:
--  Explicit deep copy: caller mutation cannot break the stored pairing.
   --  For a nonempty ORB result: Count rows, 32 columns, UInt8 C1.
   --  For an empty result: an empty Mat; no 0x32 shape is promised.
   --  The returned Mat is a new Core-owned matrix owned by the caller. It
   --  shares no storage with the set, so writing to it never changes the set,
   --  and it stays valid after the set is finalized. Matching operations
   --  read a set's descriptors directly; no copy is needed for matching.
   --  @param Features Feature set whose descriptors are copied.
   --  @return A caller-owned copy of the descriptor matrix.
   function Descriptor_Copy (Features : Feature_Set) return OpenCV.Core.Mat;

OpenCV.Features.name: Native_Version
OpenCV.Features.signature:
--  OpenCV version string (CV_VERSION) of the headers that the native
   --  Features shim was compiled against, for example "4.10.0".
   --  @return The native OpenCV version identifier.
   function Native_Version return String;

OpenCV.Features.name: Native_Backend
OpenCV.Features.signature:
--  Native OpenCV module behind this binding: "features2d" for OpenCV 4
   --  and "features" for OpenCV 5.0. The public Ada API is the same for both.
   --  @return The native backend module name.
   function Native_Backend return String;
